questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Japan and I have been studying the language for a year and a half. That's why I sought the opportunity to live and study here. I wanted to come to Tokyo because it's the biggest city in Japan, and I thought it would have the most experiences to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am very grateful to have come here. Because of my exchange, I have made friends with some local and international people. I have also improved my Japanese a lot, and I hope to use the language in my career going forwards together with my masters degree.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were many different online systems that I had to check for information leading up to and during my exchange, which was a little tedious and confusing at times. But all the information I needed was provided.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information online, and email and telephone support was made available to me by Waseda University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: All the information I needed was provided online. However, it would have been nice to have received an in-person orientation at the campus to show us around as it would have felt more welcoming.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A list of housing options where provided by the university. It was very convenient.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a little cheaper to live off campus, but with the added transportation expenses it may be worth it to live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The rooms here are generally very small. They use little insulation here so it gets cold in winter unless the heater is running constantly. The building I was assigned was old, but they take really good care of their things here so It was still in okay condition.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an online course selection system where you could read about and select the classes. The system was not that user-friendly but It worked.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and telephone support were made available. Otherwise, the support office would likely have helped as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Taking Japanese classes as an added extra course was stressful for many. I just self-studied on the side whenever I had time which worked great for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses in English were offered to both bachelors, masters, and even Ph.D. students, so perhaps they were not as deep as I was used to on the masters, but still very interesting courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Felt a lot like the same style to me.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Journalism
NPO/NGO and the future
Sustainable Development and International Development Cooperation
Regulation and Trade
Japanese Politics and Diplomacy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporary Journalism was very interesting. Its hosted by Hans Greimel, a real journalist that teaches evening classes at Waseda. He often has guest lecturers from people in the industry.

questions.answer: Did not encounter unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruits and vegetables are expensive here.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really like the system with university clubs over here. I hope to see it replicated in the West some day.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were university clubs for just about anything you can imagine. And if students want to start their own clubs they can register them with the university. However, a lot of clubs were unavailable to foreigners who don't speak Japanese.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the Intercultural Communication Center (ICC) at Waseda in building 3. They will arrange events, and also help you find a circle/club to join.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's Tokyo so there are hundreds of opportunities. Perhaps go see Asakusa in Tokyo, a famous temple. Or go to the famous Shibuya crosswalk and see that lively area.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Living here is very different from what I'm used to, but to me, it was all very interesting and refreshing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Japanese people can be rather shy, but it does not mean they don't want to interact. There are often people at the dorm to make friends with. Also, joining a circle is also a good way to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Japanese people have a particular culture of being polite and not bothering others. For example, this means not talking loudly on the trains. Foreigners often don't realize they're bothering the locals because the locals are often too shy or polite to tell them off, so be considerate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Anywhere you go you feel safe here, and every place is clean and well-maintained.  People are very polite and orderly. Also the food here is great and its relatively affordable to eat at restaurants here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Japan is a very considerate society, so be considerate in return.
2. learn some basic Japanese beforehand, the locals will appreciate your effort and a little goes a long way.
3. Make sure to experience all the sightseeing opportunities, travel destinations, and foods you can while you're there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look on YouTube for videos about living in Japan and what to experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience all the things I had heard of before coming here. Going to karaoke, Japanese arcades, eating the food here, going mountain hiking, etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exam season, when many assignments were due at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
